parts.gloss: that which is of the nature of

words.gloss: that which has the nature of surviving

literal: Things that should be done - without doing - of the miser - wealth - that which has the nature of surviving - without being - will perish.
translation: The wealth of a miser who hoards without doing what ought to be done will perish, having no chance of survival.
modern: செய்ய வேண்டிய நற்செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் பொருளைச் சேர்த்து வைக்கும் கஞ்சனுடைய செல்வம், தப்பிப் பிழைக்கும் தன்மை இல்லாமல் அழிந்து போகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the vice of miserliness and the failure to perform one's duties. The word 'செயற்பால' refers to the necessary good deeds, such as charity or supporting one's dependents, for which wealth is meant. When a person hoards wealth ('இவறியான்') without fulfilling these obligations, that wealth is doomed. The phrase 'உயற்பாலது அன்றி' emphasizes that such hoarded wealth has absolutely no means of survival and will inevitably be lost.
